thread:
samira: FYI customer (acme-corp) reports intermittent 401s and large latency spikes. They say requests from their private VPC are being routed to our EU edge instead of us-west after a recent egress change.

maria: They see ~40ms normally, now 300-800ms + auth failures. Also noticed billing counted EU region tokens.

samira: Pasting the repro and snippets they sent. @kai can you triage NAT/peering affinity?

acme-eng: repro steps:
1) curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_live_XXXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
2) sometimes get 401, then retry -> 200
Observed headers: X-Region: eu-west-1, X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.46
Source private IP: 10.250.1.12 (via onprem proxy)

samira: thanks. attaching their conntrack/logs below.

maria: logs from our EU edge when they hit EU:
```
[2026-02-18T14:02:12Z] src=34.201.12.45 dst=api.redwood.ai region=eu-west-1 auth=401 token_id=tok_live_XXXX
[2026-02-18T14:02:12Z] x-forwarded-for=203.0.113.46 proxy=onprem-proxy-1
```

kai: Looking. Initial hypothesis: their onprem proxy/TGW SNAT translates to a public IP located in EU or the TGW route propagation prefers EU hub. That would make our edge see an EU source and route to EU cluster.

jess: Also check proxy SNAT affinity + proxy pools. We've seen conntrack + TGW route timing cause egress to flip regions when peering attachments propagate different priorities.

acme-eng: their TGW config excerpt:
- default route (0.0.0.0/0) -> tgw-abc (propagated from attachments)
- attachments: attachment-usw (established 2026-02-15), attachment-eu (established 2026-02-18)
customer notes that eu attachment came up after a maintenance window.

maria: customer attached conntrack row: "tcp 6 431968 ESTABLISHED src=10.250.1.12 dst=54.36.12.99 sport=45678 dport=443 ... nat-src=203.0.113.46"

kai: That nat-src matches our EU egress IP block. We should ask them to dump proxy NAT table and BGP routes. Also want the peering propagation order and route table precedence.

samira: I ran a trace from our edge to 203.0.113.46 -> shows next-hop via eu-hub. So traffic leaves their network via EU.

jess: Mitigations to propose to customer:
- short term: force TGW route override to prefer the us-west attachment for their client subnets (update route preference).
- short term: configure proxy SNAT to use an EIP from us-west for those flows (preserve regional egress).
- medium term: add health-check based failover so token validation falls back to us-west endpoint during egress churn.

acme-eng: they will try updating TGW priority to prefer us-west and rotate SNAT EIP.

maria: I told them to collect conntrack snapshots before/after change and send pcap if behavior persists.

ops-oncall: Incident INC-20260218-87 created. Added alert rule for cross-region egress delta for tenant acme-corp.

samira: If the route override doesn't fix it we'll capture packet traces and escalate to network team. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
__notes: This document is a single Slack thread string. Messages are in chronological order and prefixed with sender name.
